title: Law of Transitory Coherence
description:
Abstract
This paper formalizes the Law of Coherence, a structural constraint governing organized systems across physical, biological, social, institutional, and knowledge domains. The law states that a system cannot project more coherence outward than it possesses internally. Apparent order that exceeds internal consistency is unstable and collapses under stress. This law is descriptive, non-predictive, domain-agnostic, observer-invariant, and falsifiable. It explains why systems that appear orderly, aligned, or trustworthy fail when internal coherence is insufficient, regardless of external enforcement, resources, or intent.
1. Scope and Non-Claims
This paper does not:
predict outcomes or timelines
assert inevitability of collapse
prescribe policy or intervention
invoke moral or ideological judgment
This paper does:
define a structural upper bound on coherence
apply across domains and scales
specify falsification conditions
describe what cannot persist
2. What Is Coherence (Operational Definition)
Coherence refers to the internal consistency of structure, meaning, alignment, and coordination within a system.
A system is coherent when:
internal rules do not contradict
signals align with actions
actions align with outcomes
feedback loops reinforce rather than conflict
Coherence is not surface order, compliance, or appearance.
3. Formal Statement of the Law
Law of Coherence (v1.0):
A system cannot project more coherence outward than it possesses internally.
4. Interpretation
This law establishes a hard upper bound.
External order cannot exceed internal alignment
Trust cannot exceed internal honesty
Stability cannot exceed internal consistency
Coordination cannot exceed internal agreement
When external coherence appears higher than internal coherence, it is illusory and collapses under load.
5. Why This Is a Constraint Law
The Law of Coherence:
forbids specific states
is invariant under effort or intent
applies regardless of scale
cannot be bypassed by enforcement
No amount of:
force
funding
authority
persuasion
can sustain coherence beyond internal consistency.
6. Observable Manifestations of Violation
When the Law of Coherence is violated, systems exhibit:
contradiction between stated values and behavior
enforcement replacing trust
increasing rule complexity
divergence between metrics and lived outcomes
fragility under stress
These are diagnostic signals, not causes.
7. Cross-Domain Examples (Non-Exhaustive)
Physical systems: structures with internal faults fail despite external reinforcement
Biological systems: organisms with internal dysregulation cannot sustain health
Institutions: organizations enforcing values they do not practice collapse under scrutiny
Markets: confidence exceeds fundamentals until sudden correction
Knowledge systems: theories with internal contradiction fail regardless of popularity
The pattern is invariant.
8. Relation to Other Laws (Boundary)
The Law of Coherence constrains how much coherence is possible.
It does not govern:
how long coherence lasts
how coherence transmits
what interventions do under confusion
Those are governed by separate laws.
9. Falsification Conditions
The Law of Coherence is falsified if a repeatable system demonstrates:
sustained external coherence exceeding internal consistency
long-term stability where internal contradiction persists
trust or alignment growing without internal alignment
If such cases exist consistently, the law is wrong.
10. Conclusion
Coherence cannot be manufactured externally. It must exist internally first. The Law of Coherence formalizes this invariant constraint across organized systems, explaining why apparent order collapses when internal alignment is absent. This law does not predict failure; it defines the boundary beyond which coherence cannot persist.
